answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with a staked reputation trellis: each identity locks a refundable bond before it can trade, and the bond is released only after a history of peer-attested work. Creating one identity is cheap, but reaching the zenith of trust, with high limits and settlement priority, takes time, consistent attestations, and locked value. A walnut-sized fake, a single throwaway account, gains almost nothing, while a Sybil farm must fund, age, and maintain thousands of bonded identities, and loses every bond when duplicates are proven.
